name: security-aws-eventbridge-bus-policy-review
intent: EventBridge producer identity, routing and consumer trust
artifacts: Bus resource policy, PutEvents caller, event fields/rules and downstream privileged consumer.
trace: Determine whether untrusted producers can set fields the consumer treats as an authenticated tenant or action instruction.
experiment: Use an owned bus or local event fixture with inert markers; compare intended producer events and a controlled spoofed authority field.
disproof: Publishing to a public intake bus can be intentional; a rule match alone is not a privileged consumer effect.
repair: Authenticate producer context and validate consumer authority, then retest rightful events and spoofed-field rejection.
branch_decisions: An event detail field claiming a tenant or user is application data, not the caller identity authenticated by the bus. Evaluate PutEvents admission, routing rule scope and consumer validation independently. Service-originated events and custom producers have different provenance; a rule match alone does not demonstrate that a protected consumer trusts a forged identity.
operational_method: Inspect PutEvents rights separately from PutRule/PutTargets and rule-update authority. Retain producer principal, source bus, selected rule and target ARN for the same synthetic event. A rule writer can redirect an otherwise authentic event; that is different from a producer forging detail fields. Verify the consumer action and intended destination with a local event-routing stub or supplied trace, without publishing real notifications.
